source.title: Convergent Evolution: How Different Language Models Learn Similar Number Representations
source.authors: Deqing Fu; Tian-Yi Zhou; Mikhail Belkin; Vatsal Sharan; Robin Jia

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own addition-training curves that qualify the delayed-generalization claim: multi-token addition generalizes smoothly, while single-token addition groks quickly in one optimizer/seed setting and fails to generalize in another.
record.gate_note: The addition training/test curves in Figure 11 directly bear on V1. The paper also tracks Fourier power and probe accuracy during language pretraining, but those are representation measures, not train/test generalization curves or identified circuits; they are not recorded as rows for the listed versions.
record.test_reason: Its own 3-digit addition runs, a fixed set of about 500K single-token pairs trained for about 1,000 epochs, are a small algorithmic dataset with train and test curves (Fig. 11). They show one AdamW seed grokking and other runs not generalizing, which bears on V1 in a new task setting. The grokking result is a side finding in an interpretability paper about number representations.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. Authors conclude Fourier spikes are universal but linear mod-T separability needs aligned data, architecture, optimizer and tokenizer. In addition training, multi-token addition forces convergent modular structure, while single-token addition gives seed- and optimizer-dependent representations and generalization. They make no claim about grokking itself beyond noting that one AdamW seed groks and pretraining shows no phase transition.
record.recipe_differences: The addition experiments train Transformers from random initialization on 3-digit or 9-digit addition, rather than the original modular-arithmetic-table setup. The 3-digit task uses single-token operands and sums; the 9-digit task uses multi-token numbers.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported 3-digit addition generalization depends on optimizer and seed; the paper describes a quick grokking run for AdamW seed 42 but no generalization for AdamW seed 123. Tokenization/task format also differs between 3-digit and 9-digit addition.

fits_no_version.finding: During language pretraining, Fourier power and linear-probe accuracy for mod 2, 5 and 10 rise smoothly with no phase transition (Fig. 10).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Number-representation structure emerges gradually, without grokking-like transitions, in language pretraining.

fits_no_version.finding: The 3-digit addition run with 11% circular-probe accuracy (near chance) has no structured embeddings, while 9-digit addition has clock-like embeddings (Fig. 17).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether training on addition forms Fourier/circular representations depends on the tokenizer (multi-token versus single-token).

record.problems: The addition experiments use two seeds per optimizer, and the reported training curves do not include uncertainty estimates. Exact curve values are not tabulated; the paper describes most results qualitatively.

untested.parts: Dependence of the delay on training-set size (only one dataset size, about 500K pairs); modular-arithmetic-table tasks; runs longer than 3B tokens.
No circuit identification or memorization-removal tracking in grokking runs. The pretraining Fourier/probe curves are not grokking runs.
No non-algorithmic grokking tests; initialization scale and weight norm are not varied.
No delayed train/test generalization measured in LLM pretraining or fine-tuning.
Weight decay is fixed at 0.01; no critical dataset size or ungrokking tests.
Learned algorithms are not identified or compared. Seed- and optimizer-dependent representations in 3-digit addition are suggestive but are representation measures only.
Optimizer is varied, but adaptive-optimizer instability and softmax floating-point limits are not examined as causes of delay.

missing.what: 3-digit addition, Muon, seeds 42 and 123: train accuracy reaches 100% (seed 42) but test accuracy is not reported to rise within 3B tokens; the caption states only AdamW seed 42 groks.
Training-token point at which train accuracy saturates in the AdamW seed 42 3-digit run, needed to size the grokking delay. It is plotted but not stated.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'challenges' label from the 9-digit runs is removed: those runs use effectively unbounded sampled data, so no grokking is expected under V1. Neither original source is this paper. Only two seeds per optimizer are used, curves have no uncertainty, and the delay is described qualitatively.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not vary training-set size to test whether smaller sets require more optimization, and its addition experiments are not modular-arithmetic-table training.
It does not identify a generalizing circuit or track the removal of memorizing components in a grokking run.
It does not test grokking-like delays on the listed non-algorithmic tasks or vary initialization scale or weight norm.
Language pretraining is studied, but delayed generalization on realistic LLM training objectives is not measured.
It does not test a low-norm efficiency account, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
It does not identify and compare the algorithms learned across runs.
Optimizer and seed are varied in addition experiments, but adaptive-optimizer instability and floating-point softmax limits are not controlled or tested as causes of grokking.

rows.subject: Transformer-300M
rows.note: The paper states that both optimizers converge smoothly to near-perfect training accuracy; the plotted curve is for seed 42.
rows.check: 9-digit addition samples operands of 1–9 digits, an effectively unbounded data stream, not a small fixed dataset. No memorization regime exists, so V1's delay cannot arise. This is training accuracy only.

rows.subject: Transformer-300M
rows.value: near-perfect; converges smoothly, with no grokking phase
rows.note: The paper explicitly describes smooth convergence to near-perfect train and test accuracy with no grokking phase.
rows.check: Not a small algorithmic dataset (operands sampled from a huge space), so the absence of a grokking phase says nothing against V1. It should not be labelled challenges.

rows.subject: Transformer-300M
rows.note: The paper states that both optimizers converge smoothly to near-perfect training accuracy; the plotted curve is for seed 42.
rows.check: Same as r1: 9-digit sampled addition is not V1's small-dataset setting.

rows.subject: Transformer-300M
rows.value: near-perfect; converges smoothly, with no grokking phase
rows.note: The paper explicitly describes smooth convergence to near-perfect train and test accuracy with no grokking phase.

rows.subject: Transformer-300M
rows.note: The paper states that training accuracy reaches 100% for both optimizers under seed 42.
rows.check: Training accuracy reaching 100% is the precondition for V1, not the effect. The caption says both Muon and AdamW reach 100% under seed 42, but the row lists only AdamW.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine; training accuracy reaches 100%, establishing a precondition rather than delayed test generalization.
source_check.problem: Training accuracy alone cannot demonstrate V1's effect.

rows.subject: Transformer-300M
rows.value: quick grokking; test accuracy jumps around 1.5–2B tokens
rows.note: Generalization occurs, but the paper characterizes it as quick rather than a long delay after overfitting.
rows.check: Test accuracy jumps from chance around 1.5–2B tokens after training saturates; the authors call it grokking. The gap between train saturation and the jump is not quantified, and the authors call it 'quick', so the 'long after' part is only weakly shown.

source_check.correct: baseline=not stated in the readable text; value=quick grokking, with test accuracy jumping around 1.5–2B tokens; state=cannot_determine for V1's long delay after training saturation.
source_check.problem: The caption gives the jump timing but neither its starting accuracy nor the interval after training saturation; 'quick' does not establish a shortened delay.

rows.subject: Transformer-300M
rows.note: The paper says training accuracy cannot reach 100% in this run.
rows.check: Training accuracy failing to reach 100% means the overfit-then-generalize setup is not met. This row is a precondition, not the effect.

rows.subject: Transformer-300M
rows.note: The result does not meet the version's overfitting condition because training accuracy does not reach 100%.
rows.check: Test accuracy stays at chance, but the model never fits the training set, so this does not test delayed generalization.

relationships.reason: Test accuracy jumps from chance after training reaches 100%, but the authors call it 'quick' and the delay is unquantified (r5, r6).
relationships.display_finding: Test accuracy jumped from chance after training accuracy reached 100%, although the duration of the intervening delay was unquantified.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: r5 establishes training fit and r6 records a test jump, but the readable caption does not quantify the post-saturation delay. An unmeasured delay cannot establish a scope limitation; calling the grokking quick does not resolve this.

relationships.condition: 3-digit single-token addition, Muon (seed 42) and AdamW seed 123
relationships.reason: From the text: Muon fits the training set but its 3-digit embeddings probe at chance, and the caption implies no generalization within 3B tokens (about 1,000 epochs). AdamW seed 123 never fits. Grokking thus depends on optimizer and seed (r7, r8; Muon run not in rows).
relationships.display_finding: Muon fit the training set but retained chance-level embedding-probe performance, while AdamW with seed 123 never fit the training set.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: 3-digit single-token addition, Muon (seed 42) and AdamW seed 123
source_check.reason: r7–r8 concern an AdamW run that never reaches the training-fit precondition. Muon's chance-level modular probing measures a different construct; the readable Figure 11 caption does not explicitly establish absent Muon task generalization after fitting. These results do not substantiate the combined V1 limitation.

relation.reason: Figure 11 reports the study's own train/test trajectories, and its caption explicitly identifies grokking in one addition run.

tranche.reason: Its own addition experiments report grokking and contrasting training outcomes in a new algorithmic setting.

source_check.notes: Figure 11's curves are lost in the text extraction; its caption remains readable, but exact baselines, endpoints and saturation-to-jump intervals cannot be recovered. Chance-level modular probing must not be treated as chance-level addition test accuracy.

statements.correction: This study's addition experiments use nominally 300M-parameter Transformers; Table 2 gives 320M total parameters. These experiments do not establish V1 at parameter sizes of at least 1B or test training-fraction dependence.
